So with maxDelegations set to 0, every delegation attempt hits the limit immediately and fails, which explains why the model can't retrieve the info — the refund requests fail the same way through this triage path, while the order desk alone works fine since it doesn't need delegation. The fix is removing that zero cap since the default should be unlimited.

My plan is to edit src/agents.ts, replacing the agents() call that includes `maxDelegations: 0` with one that omits it entirely, keeping the agent list and historyLength intact. I'll verify there's nothing else problematic in the delegation guard logic before making this edit, since I've already read the file and have a clear picture of the broken line.

The middleware source confirms it: with `maxDelegations: 0`, the guard `shared.delegationCount >= maxDelegations` is true on the first call, so every delegation returns "Delegation limit reached" without ever reaching `orderAgent` or `refundAgent`. The README says the default is unlimited. I'll remove the `maxDelegations: 0` setting from the triage agent.

text: The JSON looks valid. I didn't run the app end-to-end myself since the genkit commands should be run by the user, so I'll suggest they use `genkit start -- npm run dev` as noted in CLAUDE.md, then wrap up with a brief summary.

The support chat was failing because the triage agent had `maxDelegations: 0`, which blocks every delegation to the order and refund agents. I removed that setting in `src/agents.ts` (line 55), so triage now uses the middleware's default of unlimited delegations.

The middleware's guard checks `delegationCount >= maxDelegations` before calling any sub-agent, so 0 rejected the first delegation. The model then apologized instead of quoting the order. `orderAgent` works when called directly, which matches the report that only the chat path is broken.

`answer.json` is written at the project root. The project type-checks cleanly. I did not run the chat end to end. To check it in the Developer UI, run `genkit start -- npm run dev` and send "Where is order A-1003?" through `triage` via `tryTriage`.
